builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Neural Memory Orchestration
summary: Overseer replaces kernel heuristic prefetchers with a learned page-prefetching pipeline: an eBPF fault collector, a transformer predictor (OverNet) running on network-attached inference hardware, and a kernel enforcer that prefaults predicted pages into the target process. Its costs include dedicated inference hardware, kernel-level modifications and their operational risk, and the latency budget between fault observation and enforcement, plus per-instance feature engineering (ordinal ranks over deltas) to avoid per-workload retraining. It can fail on workloads whose access patterns are not learnable, when network or inference latency exceeds the prefetch lead time, on mispredictions that waste memory bandwidth and evict useful pages, and the reported gains come from only two fault-heavy workloads whose irregularity may not resemble the reader's inference workloads.
rationale: The system targets OS-level page prefetching for HPC workloads with kernel, eBPF, and network-attached inference prerequisites that sit outside LLM production practice on a single 24 GB GPU, so it is worth tracking but not adopting.
technique: Learned neural page prefetching via eBPF

claims.statement: Overseer replaces kernel heuristic prefetchers with a learned page-prefetching pipeline: an eBPF fault collector, a transformer predictor (OverNet) running on network-attached inference hardware, and a kernel enforcer that prefaults predicted pages into the target process. Its costs include dedicated inference hardware, kernel-level modifications and their operational risk, and the latency budget between fault observation and enforcement, plus per-instance feature engineering (ordinal ranks over deltas) to avoid per-workload retraining. It can fail on workloads whose access patterns are not learnable, when network or inference latency exceeds the prefetch lead time, on mispredictions that waste memory bandwidth and evict useful pages, and the reported gains come from only two fault-heavy workloads whose irregularity may not resemble the reader's inference workloads.

Reduces runtime by roughly 35% on Hilbert-curve traversal and by roughly an order of magnitude on dense matrix multiplication, with corresponding reductions in major-fault counts, on two page-fault-heavy workloads.
